penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Ad optimization that actually moves pipeline quality — not just volume — requires ongoing human analysis of campaign structure, audience targeting decisions, and creative iteration. There's no plug-and-play Claude prompt that replaces a skilled performance marketer's judgment loop.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Selling to GTM engineers and performance marketers at B2B SaaS companies typically requires a demo, scoping conversation, or at minimum a discovery call to establish trust and understand their ad account structure before delivering anything useful.

rationale: The buyer is real and has budget — GTM engineers at B2B SaaS companies are actively evaluating tools at $500–2k/mo. However, the core problem (pipeline quality vs. volume) requires nuanced, per-campaign human judgment that Claude cannot reliably automate end-to-end; the delivery model is inherently consulting-shaped. The combination of low buildability-as-an-autonomous-product and heavy human fulfillment requirement drops this well below viability as a factory-run micro-service.
solution_plan: This opportunity does not suit a solo non-technical operator running an autonomous Claude factory. Building a genuinely useful ad pipeline-quality optimizer requires direct access to each client's Google/Meta ad account, deep campaign analysis, creative strategy decisions, and ongoing iteration — all of which require human judgment per customer. Even if Claude could write the analysis, the operator would be doing per-client consulting work for every engagement. This is a human services business disguised as a tooling opportunity. Pass.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy_min (scored 3, floor is 7) and buildability_with_ai_min (scored 4, floor is 6). Even without penalties the build gates would cap this at validate. With penalties the total drops to 3.1, which is below the validate threshold.
